retrieval_verdict: at chance — exact partner-patch pick needs finer-than-residue resolution
verdict: The REAL version — real coordinates, real residue chemistry, a real contrastive net trained by gradient descent, validated on complexes held OUT by GroupKFold — gives a TWO-SIDED honest result. WHAT WORKS: pairwise DISCRIMINATION. On held-out complexes the trained encoder separates true interface patch-pairs from non-contacting pairs at AUC 0.65, versus 0.50 for the untrained raw-feature-cosine baseline — so learning surface COMPLEMENTARITY adds +0.15 of real, generalising signal, and (unlike the random-weight mock) the training genuinely earns it. WHAT MOSTLY DOESN'T: exact partner-patch RETRIEVAL. Given a patch, finding its actual partner patch among hard decoys (other surface patches on the SAME partner protein) is only WEAKLY above chance — top-1 2.5% vs 1.7% chance, top-5 11.8% vs 8.3% chance (a consistent but small ~1.4x lift in every fold) — because pinpointing the ONE right patch among dozens of near-interface patches needs finer spatial resolution than residue-level features carry. So the model can say 'do these two patches look complementary' better than coin-flip, but it can only barely concentrate the true partner toward the top of a panel, not reliably pick it out. HONEST LIMITS driving this ceiling: patches are residue-level with geometry-from-atoms + chemistry-from-identity — NO MSMS molecular-surface mesh and NO APBS electrostatics, so this is a much coarser surface than real MaSIF (which uses true surfaces + Poisson-Boltzmann fields and reports stronger discrimination AND usable retrieval); it is trained on the 344 real complexes we have, not 20,000 proteins (complementarity training needs COMPLEXES for interface labels — monomers have none — so the 20k-monomer 'proteome DB' is a downstream fetch that would NOT change this validated accuracy); and this is surface complementarity, near-field STRUCTURE, NOT validated discovery of a NOVEL PPI (still needs docking + experiment, as ppi_screen concluded). Bottom line vs the mock: the mock printed 99%-confidence proteome hits from random weights on random data; the REAL model, honestly, gets a MODEST discrimination signal (0.65 AUC, +0.15 over untrained) and AT-CHANCE exact retrieval — the truth is less impressive than the mock's fiction, and that gap IS the point. Real MaSIF-grade performance needs the molecular-surface + electrostatics tooling this environment lacks.
